mainEntity.name: How much does a Land Rover Defender 90 2.8i engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt or reconditioned engine replacement for a Land Rover Defender 90 2.8i typically ranges from £5,000 to £8,000 for supply only, depending on the specialist and the extent of upgrades included. Used engines start around £2,000 but carry higher risk, while rebuilt units include upgraded components and a 12-month warranty.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of a failing M52B28 engine in a Land Rover Defender 90 2.8i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning signs in the Land Rover Defender 90 2.8i are a distinct rattling noise from the front of the engine at specific RPMs, known as VANOS rattle, and unexplained coolant loss. You should also check for sweet-smelling exhaust, white smoke, or oil residue around the valve cover and oil filter housing.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a classic Land Rover Defender 90 2.8i?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, given the strong classic car market, a well-maintained Land Rover Defender 90 2.8i typically holds a value between £8,000 and £15,000, making a £5,000 to £8,000 rebuilt engine a financially sound investment. A rebuilt engine restores reliability, preserves resale value, and is significantly cheaper than purchasing a newer 4x4.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Land Rover Defender 90 2.8i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional supply and fit service for a Land Rover Defender 90 2.8i typically takes 2 to 4 days, depending on the specialist's workload and whether any ancillary components like the cooling system are being upgraded simultaneously. Sourcing a quality rebuilt unit may add a few days, so always confirm the exact turnaround time with your chosen specialist.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the Land Rover Defender 90 2.8i and the Td5 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Land Rover Defender 90 2.8i uses a naturally aspirated BMW M52B28 inline-six petrol engine, prioritising smoothness, refinement, and mechanical simplicity. In contrast, the Td5 is a turbocharged inline-five diesel focused on low-end torque and fuel economy, though it carries its own known electrical issues.

historyTimeline.h2: Land Rover Defender 90 2.8i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the Land Rover Defender 90 2.8i launched in the late 1990s, it offered a refined, powerful alternative to the traditional diesel workhorses, bringing smooth inline-six petrol performance to the iconic short-wheelbase 4x4.

milestones.description: Introduction of the BMW M52B28 2.8L inline-6 petrol engine, replacing older Rover V8 options in select markets for improved refinement and emissions compliance.
Peak production year for the M52-powered Defender 90, featuring updated engine management and continued use in County and Station Wagon trims.
Final year of the M52B28 in the classic Defender 90 lineup before the transition to newer Td5 and later Puma engine architectures dominated the range.

commonProblems.h2: Land Rover Defender 90 2.8i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW M52B28 inline-six in the Land Rover Defender 90 2.8i is generally regarded as a robust and smooth powerplant, but age-related wear on cooling and valvetrain components is common. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Cooling System Failure - Why the Land Rover Defender 90 2.8i M52B28 Overheats
problems.rootCause: Plastic components in the cooling system (expansion tank, water pump housing, thermostat) become brittle with age and heat cycles, leading to coolant leaks and subsequent overheating.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace expansion tank, water pump, thermostat, and hoses with upgraded metal/composite parts.
repairOptions.longevity: Extends life significantly if caught before overheating damage occurs.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded cooling components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if the engine has already suffered thermal damage or warped heads.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Land Rover Defender 90 2.8i of relevant age (1997-2001) currently holds a UK market value of approximately £8,000-£15,000 [THIRD-PARTY - Auto Trader / Classic Car market observations], with well-maintained examples commanding higher premiums. At this value band, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine replacement typically justifies the premium via warranty and reliability, preserving the vehicle's classic status and resale value.
problems.recommendation: If your Land Rover Defender 90 2.8i is running hot but has not suffered catastrophic thermal damage, a comprehensive preventative cooling system refresh by a specialist is the most cost-effective route. However, if the engine has already overheated and warped the cylinder head, a rebuilt replacement is the only reliable long-term solution.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M52B28 Land Rover Defender 90 2.8i engine prices

problems.h4: VANOS Unit Rattle & Oil Leaks - Why the Land Rover Defender 90 2.8i M52B28 Loses Refinement
problems.rootCause: The single-VANOS system's internal seals degrade over time, causing a distinct rattling noise at specific RPMs, alongside common oil leaks from the valve cover and oil filter housing gaskets.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Disassemble VANOS unit, replace degraded seals with upgraded Viton seals, and refresh external gaskets.
repairOptions.longevity: Highly effective at restoring smooth idle and eliminating rattle without full engine removal.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded VANOS and sealing components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended only if the rattling has progressed to catastrophic camshaft or timing chain damage.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above, the £8,000-£15,000 value band of a classic Land Rover Defender 90 2.8i makes targeted repairs like a VANOS rebuild highly viable. A full engine replacement is rarely justified for VANOS rattle alone unless secondary damage has occurred.
problems.recommendation: Do not ignore a VANOS rattle, but do not panic either. A specialist VANOS rebuild kit is a well-documented, cost-effective fix that restores the smooth, torquey character of the Land Rover Defender 90 2.8i without requiring a full engine replacement.
